title: Binary search trees
summary: Binary search, but for data that changes.

cards.title: Sorted, but cheap to insert
cards.body:
A sorted array finds things fast (binary search) but inserting shifts everything: O(n). A **binary search tree** keeps the same "go left or right" idea in a structure where inserting is cheap.

Rule: everything in a node's **left** subtree is smaller, everything on the **right** is bigger or equal.
`std::unique_ptr<TreeNode>&`: a reference to the owning pointer. When we reach an empty spot we assign straight into it, so no parent bookkeeping is needed.

cards.title: The catch: balance
cards.body: Insert 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in that order and every node goes right: the "tree" is a linked list and search is O(n). Self-balancing trees (red-black, AVL) fix this; `std::map` and `std::set` are usually red-black trees.

cards.question: Insert 5, 2, 8, 1 into an empty BST. What is the left child of 2?
cards.explain: 5 is the root. 2 < 5 goes left. 8 > 5 goes right. 1 < 5, then 1 < 2: left of 2.
